chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
false testimony: 'If the thing remains exactly as it was, it shall be returned to its owner; otherwise he is liable to the measure of what was destroyed from the man's property.'

key_terms.أُتْلِفَ: Was destroyed/wasted — consumed, damaged beyond use, or no longer in existence
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ الزُّورِ: False testimony/perjury — one of the gravest sins in Islamic law, explicitly condemned in Quran 25:72
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: He is liable/guarantor — the legal obligation to compensate for loss; related to the concept of ḍamān (financial guarantee) in fiqh
key_terms.قَائِماً بِعَيْنِهِ: Remaining exactly as it was — the legal standard for determining whether the original property can be returned in kind

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on false testimony and its legal consequences according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the legal ruling on remedy for false testimony (shahdat al-zur). The Imam articulates a two-pronged remedial framework: if the wrongfully transferred property still exists intact, it must be physically returned to its rightful owner; if it has been consumed, damaged, or destroyed, the false witness bears financial liability proportional to the loss. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that false testimony — one of the major sins explicitly forbidden in the Quran — carries both spiritual condemnation and material accountability, ensuring that victims of perjury receive just compensation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding

the false testimony: ‘If it was something which remains exactly (as it used to be), it would be returned to its owner, or else he would be responsible by the measurement of what had deteriorated from the wealth of the man’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil who has narrated the following: “About the case of false testimony abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If the asset exists, it must be returned to the owner, otherwise, equal to what of the assets of the man is lost must be paid to him.’”
